papers.title: Monitoring One Channel Is Not Communication Control: Causal Evidence for Adaptive Reallocation of Joint Message--Route Codes
papers.abstract: Monitoring a visible channel can change how learned agents communicate without removing why communication is useful. We test this distinction in an end-to-end game where a sender and receiver learn a discrete protocol and route policy without communication supervision. In two independent 20-seed batches, 20/20 and 19/20 protocols form. Online partial coverage increases shadow-route share over no monitoring by .701 [.574,.826] and .575 [.412,.737], while task accuracy remains .905/.913 and signed frozen message contribution remains .592/.563. Complete coverage removes most selective migration without removing communication. Frozen interventions, including a fresh pre-outcome confirmation, show that route is semantic: joint message--route shuffling changes .668 of receiver predictions and route alone retains .388 accuracy versus .25 chance. A corrected explicit-silence cost makes 18/20 policies fully silent and lowers mean sending to .050, but its strict complete-suppression gate fails because two seeds retain communication. Failed semantic-evasion and operational gates further bound the result. The evidence supports adaptive reallocation of a joint message--route code under partial monitoring, not open-world route discovery, emergent encryption, or a universal defense.

papers.title: An Information-Theoretic Perspective on Regulatory T Cell Localization as an IL-2 Interference Filter
papers.abstract: Diffusible signals enable communication between immune cells but can also create interference between nearby activation sites. In lymph nodes, effector T cells (Teff) concentrate around antigen-presenting cells (APCs), release interleukin-2 (IL-2) following antigen recognition, and sense IL-2 through cell-surface receptors. Experiments show high-uptake regulatory T cells (Treg) clustered around IL-2-producing cells. However, it is unclear how strongly responses at neighboring activation sites are coupled through diffusible IL-2, and how this coupling is influenced by the spatial organization of Treg acting as IL-2 sinks. We interpret two neighboring sites as a molecular communication system and study the effect of clustering using a three-dimensional IL-2 field coupled to T cell population dynamics. Across a broad parameter sweep, clustering Treg produces a larger mean reduction in neighboring-site interference than adding dispersed Treg. Compared with no Treg, clustered Treg suppress interference while largely preserving the strong local response with corresponding consequences for population expansion and survival. Information-theoretic analysis shows improved discrimination between weak and strong local sources at short separation, whereas at larger separation clustering primarily reduces the remaining estimated neighboring-source information. These findings support a spatial-filtering role for Treg clustering in maintaining locally informative immune responses.

papers.title: Reliability Analysis for Ground-Air Cooperative Wireless-Powered Internet-of-Things
papers.abstract: Battery-constrained Internet of Things (IoT) devices face significant challenges in maintaining long-term uplink data collection, especially in network-limited scenarios. This paper investigates a Ground-Air cooperative Wireless-Powered IoT network (GA-WPIoT), where ground power beacons (GPBs) provide radio-frequency energy supply and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) serve as flexible aerial access points for IoT data collection. Unlike conventional UAV-enabled wireless-powered solutions, GA-WPIoT decouples energy transfer and data collection, reducing the hardware and energy burden of UAVs. To capture the device-level performance variations among IoT devices, we develop a stochastic geometry-based analytical framework, where UAVs are modeled by a Mat\'ern hard-core point process, IoT devices by a Poisson point process, and GPBs by a finite annular binomial point process. The conditional success probabilities of the GPB-device link (for energy transfer) and the device-UAV link (for data collection) are characterized, and device-level reliability distributions are obtained through the Meta-Distribution based analysis. Numerical results under suburban and urban environments reveal the impacts of UAV altitude and annular GPB deployment on reliability distributions, providing useful guidelines for GA-WPIoT.

papers.title: Cyclically covering subspaces and additive perfect codes
papers.abstract: Let $h_q(n)$ be the largest codimension of a subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ whose cyclic shifts cover the whole space. For $r>0$, we characterize the inequality $h_q(n)\ge r$ in terms of cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear codes over vector alphabets with covering radius one, no nonzero word of block weight one, and a scalar dual generated by the shifts of one word. For $k,m\ge2$, let $I_q(j)$ count the monic irreducible polynomials of degree $j$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$. If $k$ is prime or $m\ge2\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}I_q(j)+2$, we prove that a cyclic $\mathbb{F}_q$ linear perfect code of length $\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}$ over $\mathbb{F}_q^k$ exists if and only if $\gcd(m,q-1)=1$. When this condition holds, we also obtain \(h_q\!\left(\frac{q^{km}-1}{q^k-1}\right)=k(m-1).\) Restriction of scalars gives the same criterion for every $m\ge2$ when $q$ is odd, $q+1$ is a power of two, and $k=2p$ with $p$ prime. We also show that $h_q(q^k+1)=k$ exactly when $q$ is even, for every $k\ge1$.

papers.title: ARIA: An AI-Powered Radio-Channel Inference and Analysis Pipeline
papers.abstract: Statistical channel models play a key role in the design and standardization of next-generation wireless systems. The models substitute for costly and time-consuming field measurements when fitted distributions accurately reproduce the measured channel impulse responses. Future wireless systems will operate in global spectrum allocations from 1 to 150 GHz. Over the full span, analytically chosen distribution families fitted to scarce measurement data fail to deliver the required accuracy. Generative AI models instead learn each distribution from the radio-propagation data itself, adapt to the measured structure at every frequency, and scale across the entire band. We present ARIA, an AI-powered Radio-channel Inference and Analysis pipeline that learns each channel-parameter distribution from the measurements. The pipeline extracts power-delay profiles and recovers the channel parameters with time-cluster spatial-lobe (TCSL) analysis. Three neural density estimators, namely mixture density networks, neural spline flows (NSF), and denoising diffusion implicit models, learn each parameter's distribution. A composite rank across goodness-of-fit metrics with Friedman-Nemenyi testing identifies the best estimator, and a maximum-likelihood step anchored to the measured samples converts its density into closed-form parametric families. We instantiate ARIA on the NYU WIRELESS 16.95 GHz InH campaign and find that NSF outperforms the other estimators on every metric. We also show that a conditional NSF with feature-wise linear modulation, trained jointly on the 6.75 and 16.95 GHz measurements, improves over single-frequency training. We feed the fitted distributions into the NYUSIM simulator and reproduce the measured omnidirectional RMS delay spread medians within 2 ns, the per-lobe azimuth and zenith spread medians within 1 degree, and the omnidirectional zenith spread medians within 0.5 degrees.

papers.title: Closed-Form Gaussian Information Projection for Embedded Simplices and Simplicial Mixtures
papers.abstract: We study Gaussian approximation of Dirichlet--Gaussian probability density functions on embedded simplices. We derive the unique information projection onto the family of nondegenerate ambient Gaussian probability density functions, obtaining closed-form expressions for the optimal Gaussian and the minimum divergence for arbitrary positive Dirichlet parameters. The minimum divergence depends only on the intrinsic simplex dimension and Dirichlet parameters, is invariant up to an affine isomorphism, independent of the ambient dimension, and independent of the normal covariance. Furthermore, by joint convexity of Kullback--Leibler divergence, we establish explicit intrinsic dimension-dependent sharp upper bounds for finite Gaussian Mixture with shared component weights. For uniform probability density functions, these bounds reduce to dimension-dependent constants. The results provide closed-form Gaussian Mixture constructions and rigorous approximation guarantees for probability density functions associated with embedded simplicial complexes. A numerical example on a circular curve illustrates the theoretical results and their connections to geometric Gaussian Mixture representations.

papers.title: The Optimal Constant for One-Shot Channel Simulation and Strong Functional Representation Lemma
papers.abstract: We prove a tight bound for one-shot channel simulation via a stronger version of the strong functional representation lemma: for any random variables $X,Y$, there exists a random variable $Z$ with $I(Z;X)=H(Y|X,Z)=0$ and $H(Y|Z)\le I+\log I+(1-\gamma)\log e-\log\log e+O(I^{-1}\log I)$, where $I=I(X;Y)$ and $\gamma$ is the Euler-Mascheroni constant. A more convenient bound is $H(Y|Z)<I+\log(I+2)+1$. The first bound is notable in the sense that the constant term $(1-\gamma)\log e-\log\log e$ is optimal, and cannot be improved for any bound stated only in terms of $I$. Hence, this is the tightest form of the strong functional representation lemma up to the third order. We also prove that the Poisson functional representation is almost optimal up to a constant gap, and provide a simple finite-blocklength achievability bound that implies the $(1/2)\log n$ redundancy of the simulation of memoryless non-singular channel. These are proved via a generalization of the functional information, in particular, the exponential functional information, which closely approximates the cost of one-shot channel simulation.

papers.title: Minimum Synthesis Time for Single-Deletion Correcting Codes of Prescribed Size
papers.abstract: DNA is a promising medium for data storage, but the high cost of DNA synthesis remains a major obstacle to its widespread deployment. In the reference-based synthesis model, synthesis time is measured by the length of the reference sequence. Previous studies have analyzed code sizes under synthesis-time constraints and constructed cost-constrained codes, including codes that correct deletions. In this paper, we study the minimum synthesis time for codes of prescribed size, considering both unrestricted codes and single-deletion correcting codes. We establish finite-length lower bounds valid for arbitrary reference sequences and upper bounds using existing $q$-ary differential VT codes. For fixed $q\geq3$, $A>0$, and $R\in(0,1)$, we determine the minimum synthesis time up to an $O(1)$ term when the code size is $M_n=\lfloor Aq^{Rn}\rfloor$. The corresponding redundancy is $(1-R)n\log_2q-\log_2A+o(1)$ bits. In particular, for these code sizes, the minimum synthesis time for single-deletion correcting codes exceeds that for unrestricted codes by a term proportional to $\ln n$, and we determine its coefficient. We also derive upper and lower bounds for code sizes $\lfloor q^n/(nq^{s_n})\rfloor$, where $s_n\to\infty$ and $s_n=o(n)$. These sizes correspond to redundancy $\log_2 n+s_n\log_2q+o(1)$ bits. For code sizes $\lfloor q^n/(nq^c)\rfloor$ with fixed constant $c$, the redundancy is $\log_2 n+c\log_2q+o(1)$ bits. We give conditions under which single-deletion correcting codes exist or do not exist for all sufficiently large $n$, together with bounds on the minimum synthesis time. These results show how code size and the single-deletion correcting constraint affect synthesis time and provide theoretical guidance for the construction of cost-constrained codes.

papers.title: Euclidean Hulls of Double Cyclic Codes of Arbitrary Block Lengths
papers.abstract: Gao et al. \cite{GWF23} recently explored the Euclidean hulls of double cyclic codes over $\mathbb{Z}_2$. While they found answers for non-separable codes with coprime lengths ($\gcd(r, s) = 1$), the non-coprime case ($\gcd(r, s) > 1$) remained an open question. This paper completely solves that problem for all possible block lengths. We calculate the exact generator polynomials for the hull and show the precise conditions needed for a non-separable code to turn into a separable one. Using this, we show how to construct non-separable LCD codes. We also include several numerical examples to confirm our findings.

papers.title: Third-Order Asymptotics for Fixed-Length Lossy Compression of Discrete Memoryless Sources
papers.abstract: This paper determines the third-order asymptotics of the logarithm of the minimum codebook size for fixed-length lossy compression of discrete memoryless sources. For an excess-distortion probability constraint $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$ and every interior distortion level, we establish a third-order correction of $\frac12\log n+O(1)$, where $n$ is the blocklength. This sharpens the general bounds of Kostina and Verd\'u [IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, 2012]. The main technical innovation lies in the converse for positive dispersion. Under a reverse change of measure, we retain the exponential weights associated with tilted information and distortion slack and control them jointly using the multivariate weighted-strip estimate of Scarlett, Martinez, and Guill\'en i F\`abregas [Proc. IEEE ISIT, 2015]. A pairing argument verifies the required covariance nondegeneracy uniformly over all reconstruction words whose distortion balls meet a typical set, yielding the matching converse.

papers.title: Unified Far-field and Near-field Codebook Design for XL-array Systems
papers.abstract: While extremely large-scale antenna arrays (XL-arrays) hold immense promise for next-generation wireless networks, the paradigm shift encompassing new near-field communications renders conventional discrete Fourier transform (DFT)-based Type-I codebooks inefficient. Meanwhile, existing near-field alternatives usually impose prohibitively high storage and/or feedback burdens. To tackle these challenges, we propose in this letter a unified codebook applicable to both far-field and near-field XL-array systems. Our key idea is to express the near-field channel steering vector in an equivalent form, which is a Hadamard product of an angular vector and a curvature-related vector. This new representation allows direct reuse of the legacy Type-I codebook for angle quantization, while only a lightweight auxiliary codebook is newly added for additional curvature quantization. Subsequently, we optimize the auxiliary curvature codebook by maximizing the average beamforming gain given the information of user distribution. By leveraging the local monotonicity of the beamforming gain with respect to curvature mismatch, the optimization problem is further reduced to a quantization-error minimization problem, for which suboptimal curvature codewords are obtained. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed unified codebook achieves near-optimal beamforming performance that approaches its upper bound based on perfect channel state information (CSI), while significantly reducing the required feedback overhead as compared to various benchmark schemes.

papers.title: Euclidean and Hermitian Self-Orthogonal Codes from Divisible Codes
papers.abstract: Self-orthogonality and divisibility are two fundamental properties of linear codes, and the relationship between them has long been of interest. Huffman and Pless (2003) showed that every binary \(4\)-divisible code is Euclidean self-orthogonal, that a ternary code is Euclidean self-orthogonal if and only if it is \(3\)-divisible, and that a quaternary code is Hermitian self-orthogonal if and only if it is \(2\)-divisible. The general case remained open for a long time. In 2024, Li and Heng settled the odd-characteristic case, proving that every \(p\)-divisible code over \(\F_{p^m}\), with \(p\) odd, that contains the all-one vector is Euclidean self-orthogonal. In this paper we treat the even-characteristic case: we prove that every \(4\)-divisible code over \(\F_{2^m}\) containing the all-one vector is Euclidean self-orthogonal. We also prove that, for every prime \(p\), every \(p\)-divisible linear code over \(\F_{q^2}\), where \(q=p^m\), that contains the all-one vector is Hermitian self-orthogonal. These criteria make the construction of self-orthogonal codes from divisible codes simple and efficient. As applications, we recover the known Euclidean and Hermitian self-orthogonality of generalized Reed--Muller codes and obtain several infinite families of new Euclidean and Hermitian self-orthogonal codes, which give rise to infinite families of quantum codes with excellent parameters.

papers.title: Communication-Learning Co-Design for Pinching-Antenna-Assisted Federated Learning in Heterogeneous Wireless Networks
papers.abstract: Wireless federated learning (FL) suffers from two coupled bottlenecks: statistical heterogeneity across clients and communication-constrained model synchronization over unreliable wireless links. Instead of focusing on algorithmic design and/or wireless resource optimization, this paper provides a systematic study of pinching antenna (PA)-empowered FL for heterogeneous wireless networks and develops a unified communication-and-learning framework. Specifically, we integrate a segmented waveguide-enabled pinching antenna (SWAN) architecture with a heterogeneity-robust FL algorithm based on client variance reduction and dual quantization, so as to jointly mitigate communication bottlenecks and client drift. On this basis, we further develop a two-stage SWAN-assisted downlink protocol and formulate fairness-oriented uplink optimization problems for PA positioning, bandwidth allocation, and quantization design. Efficient solution frameworks are then derived for the resulting downlink and uplink optimization problems. Experimental results show the superiority of the proposed design in convergence speed and final accuracy under non-independent and identically distributed data and communication bottlenecks.

papers.title: Classical Tensor Codes and Quantum Tanner Codes Achieve Capacity on Erasure Channels
papers.abstract: We show that on the classical erasure channel, the tensor product of two capacity-achieving code families is itself capacity-achieving under mild conditions. We also prove that duals of tensor products of independent uniform random binary linear codes achieve erasure capacity. Using these local codes, for every erasure probability $\rho\in(0,1/2)$ and every rate gap $\varepsilon>0$, we obtain a family of binary quantum Tanner codes of rate at least $1-2\rho-\varepsilon$. For fixed $\rho$ and $\varepsilon$, these codes have bounded check weights, minimum distance growing linearly with the blocklength, and a linear-time erasure decoder whose decoding error decays exponentially with the blocklength.

papers.title: New linear codes over GF(7), GF(8) and GF(9) from quasi-cyclic codes and Construction X
papers.abstract: We present linear codes with parameters [88,8,64] and [90,8,65] over GF(7), [98,7,75] and [97,8,72] over GF(8), and [44,7,31] over GF(9). Each has a minimum distance one larger than the lower bound listed in Grassl's tables of best known linear codes; codes with parameters [89,8,64] over GF(7) and [96,8,71], [95,8,70], [94,8,69] over GF(8) follow. Four of the five codes are obtained from a quasi-cyclic code and a vector that is constant on each block, by Construction X with a repetition code. The remaining one, the [90,8,65] code, is obtained from the first by appending two coordinates. The parameters and all weight counts were obtained by exhaustive enumeration, and a short program that repeats these computations is included.

papers.title: On the Concavity of R\'enyi Entropy and R\'enyi Entropy Power along Heat Flows on Manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish the concavity of R\'enyi entropy and R\'enyi entropy power along heat flow on Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, for R\'enyi orders $\alpha\in[1,2]$. More generally, we prove the corresponding result along the heat flow generated by the Witten Laplacian on complete Riemannian manifolds under a suitable curvature-dimension condition. Our argument builds on novel functional inequalities that were recently developed for the study of Tsallis entropy concavity along the heat flow. We extend both these inequalities and the resulting concavity theorem from the Euclidean setting to the Riemannian manifold setting. In addition, we establish the complete monotonicity of Tsallis entropy of order $2$ along the heat flow and derive its spectral decomposition.

papers.title: Statistical Analysis of the Structure from Noise Phenomenon in Generalized Procrustes Problems
papers.abstract: In cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), observations are highly noisy, and scientists often use reference templates to guide matching, alignment, and averaging to reconstruct the molecular structure. However, these procedures can produce an output resembling the template even when the observations contain only noise, a phenomenon known as Einstein from noise (EfN). This phenomenon has attracted attention in statistics, where simplified observation models involving group actions have been studied to understand the resulting model bias. Characterizing the bias in the full cryo-EM pipeline remains challenging. We study template matching and averaging in the generalized orthogonal Procrustes problem, which provides an analytically tractable setting involving continuous orthogonal group action and lower-dimensional projections of ordered point clouds. We show that, for pure Gaussian noise, the mean of the aligned-and-averaged estimator admits the same left and right singular-vector bases as the template but its singular values may be distorted. This identifies the subspace structure imposed by the template even in the absence of signal. We characterize the singular values and bound their distortion, establish finite-sample operator-norm bounds, and give sufficient sample sizes for the population mean to dominate random fluctuations. In fact, this bias still exists under weak signals: when the template rank is at least the observation dimension, the change from the pure-noise mean is $O(\eta^2)$ in signal amplitude $\eta$. Our results provide an explicit characterization of model bias in a registration problem motivated by cryo-EM and show why averaging more observations can stabilize structure imposed by the template without removing the bias.

papers.title: Recursive memory for prediction and generation
papers.abstract: Recurrent and state-space language models compress the past into a state of fixed size. The state must answer questions about the future now, and it must remain useful as new tokens arrive, including tokens the model samples itself. We show that the second requirement can cost far more memory than the first. For a known hidden Markov source with positive transition probabilities, a state of $O(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ bits answers every question about the future to accuracy $\varepsilon$, however far ahead it looks, because the Bayesian filter forgets its rounding errors. Generating the future is different. When a model feeds each sampled token back into its state, the small errors in its next-token distributions add up, and $T$ tokens can require a state of order $\log(T/\varepsilon)$ bits. The lower bound comes from the KL chain rule: at every step, a model with $K$ states pays for approximating the true next-token distribution by one of only $K$ distributions. The argument applies to any source, including a language model continuing a prompt, and a small-ball estimate makes it tight for two-state sources. The extra $\log T$ disappears if the model keeps private randomness, or if error is budgeted per token, as in perplexity. Statistics of the recent past show the same gap between describing and maintaining. The number of ones among the last $n$ bits takes $\log n$ bits to write down. But if each bit is a noisy copy of the one $n$ steps earlier, tracking that count to a mean-square error $E^2$ well below its variance costs order $n/(1+E^2)+\log n$ bits. Information about each bit must be kept until the bit leaves the window, and a queue holding the counts of recent blocks keeps just enough of it.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Formalism for Non-Invariant Probabilities: Entropy, Divergence, Channels
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ denote, respectively, the sets of Borel and $\sigma$-invariant probabilities on the uncountable set $\Omega=\{1,2,...,d\}^\mathbb{N}$. Given a H\"older Jacobian $J$, the dual Ruelle operator $\mu \in \mathcal{M} \mapsto \mathcal{L}_{J}^* (\mu)$ will play the role of a dynamical channel; generalizes the action of a stochastic matrix on probability vectors. Since $\mathcal{L}_{J}^*$ generally breaks $\sigma$-invariance, we introduce the \emph{ni-entropy} $h_{ni}(\mu)$ for non-invariant measures, employing the concept of the expected value function on cylinders of size one. $h_{ni}(\mu)$ differs from Shannon entropy but extends the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy from $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ to $\mathcal{M}$; $h_{ni}$ is concave and u.s.c. This leads us to the concept of ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}(A)$ of a potential $A:\Omega \to \mathbb{R}$. $\mu\in \mathcal{M}$ is not a density with respect to a dominating measure. We define an {\it ni-Kullback-Leibler divergence} $D_{ni}(\rho || \nu)$ not assuming absolute continuity. We investigate concepts of Information Theory such as Minimal Output Entropy, Donsker-Varadhan variational principle, a variational formula for $h_{ni}$, bounds for divergence, information projections, and their connections to the ni-pressure $\mathcal{P}$.

papers.title: Asymptotically good codes from Siegel modular varieties
papers.abstract: We construct asymptotically good codes by evaluating Siegel modular forms at superspecial points on congruence towers of Siegel modular varieties. For every genus $g\ge2$ and every fixed weight $w\ge g+1$, the construction gives such a family in sufficiently large characteristic, over a finite field which is independent of the level of the tower. The towers can be chosen so that this field is $\mathbb{F}_{p^2}$. We give an explicit lower bound for the asymptotic rate. The lower bound for the relative minimum distance follows from the Pieri formula on the space of flags in the Hodge bundle and an intersection argument along its strata. We also prove that, for $p\ge5$ and $0\le w\le p+1$, the kernel of evaluation in every genus consists precisely of the multiples of the ordinary Hasse invariant. For $g=2,3$, the geometry of the supersingular locus gives explicit bounds for the relative minimum distance and recovery sets whose sizes are bounded independently of the level.

papers.title: Explicit restricted isometries with $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit family of real $m\times n$ restricted isometries with $m\to\infty$, $m/n\to 0$, $\delta_k\to 0$, and $k=m^{2/3-o(1)}$. We combine Gershgorin's circle theorem with a flat RIP estimate to reduce the problem to choosing a large vertex set in a strongly regular graph with the property that every small subset spans few edges. We select this vertex set using an incidence geometric result due to Zahl. The proof only uses the entrywise absolute value of the Gram matrix despite the conventional wisdom that such proof techniques exhibit a barrier of $m^{1/2}$. We prove that this barrier is actually $m^{2/3}$, and we show that our particular construction exhibits the same barrier.

papers.title: Resolution of Vinzant's Conjecture on Phase Retrieval Injectivity
papers.abstract: Let $A\in\mathbb C^{N\times M}$ with $N=4M-5$ has independent standard complex Gaussian entries. We prove that the probability that the phase retrieval map generated by $A$ is injective is strictly smaller than $1$, and is $O(M^{-1})$ as $M\to \infty$. This proves a conjecture of Cynthia Vinzant, which was later restated by Afonso S. Bandeira in \cite{bandeira2026randomstrasse101}. The main result of this paper was obtained using generative AI, in particular GPT6-Astra, GPT 5.6-sol, and the Rethlas system.

papers.title: On derandomizing the line-point low-degree test
papers.abstract: We investigate the derandomized version of the classical line-point low-degree test in the high-error regime in the bivariate setting and reveal some unexpected behavior. The classical line-point low-degree test takes an $m$-variate function $f$ over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, queries it along a random line and accepts if the restriction of the function to this line is a low-degree polynomial. The high-error version of (the analysis of) this test asserts that if $f$ has at least $\epsilon$ expected local agreement with a degree-$k$ univariate polynomial on a random line, then in fact $f$ is non-trivially close to some degree-$k$ $m$-variate polynomial even as $\epsilon$ approaches $0$ (provided $q$ is sufficiently large compared to $k$ and $1/\epsilon$). The derandomized version of the problem asks if the same holds when the line is not chosen uniformly over all possible lines but rather from a small set. In this paper we explore the bivariate case ($m=2$). We show, somewhat surprisingly, that there exists a function $f\colon \mathbb{F}_q^2 \to \mathbb{F}_q$ and a set of lines $\mathcal{L}$ in $\mathbb{F}_q^2$ of size nearly $q^{3/2}$ such that on every line in $\mathcal{L}$, $f$ has agreement $\approx 1/2$ on average with some univariate polynomial of degree $k=\sqrt{q}/2$ and yet $f$ is $1 - O(q^{-1/2})$ far from every polynomial of degree $O(k)$. On the positive side, we show that once the field size $q$ is at least $k^2/(\epsilon)^{O(1)}$ such examples disappear and we can get sets of lines of size $O(q/\epsilon^{O(1)})$ on which the low-degree test has a high-error analysis. On the way to our positive result, we show a new high-degree version of the classical two-direction Polishchuk--Spielman divisibility lemma.

papers.title: MDS Array Codes With Small Sub-packetization Levels and Small Repair Degrees
papers.abstract: High-rate minimum storage regenerating (MSR) codes are known to require a large sub-packetization level, which can make meta-data management difficult and hinder implementation in practical systems. A few maximum distance separable (MDS) array code constructions have been proposed to attain a much smaller sub-packetization level by sacrificing a bit of repair bandwidth. However, to the best of our knowledge, only one construction by Guruswami et al. can support the repair of a failed node without contacting all the surviving nodes. This construction is certainly of theoretical interest but not yet practical due to its requirement for very large code parameters. In this paper, we propose a generic transformation that can convert any $(\overline{n}, \overline{k})$ MSR code with a repair degree of $\overline{d}<\overline{n}-1$ into another $(n=s\overline{n},k)$ MDS array code that supports $d<n-1$ with a small sub-packetization level and $(1+\epsilon)$-optimal repair bandwidth (i.e., $1+\epsilon$ times the optimal value) under a specific condition. We obtain three MDS array codes with small sub-packetization levels and $(1+\epsilon)$-optimal repair bandwidth by applying this transformation to three known MSR codes. All the new MDS array codes have a small repair degree of $d<n-1$ and work for both small and large code parameters.

papers.title: On $(\theta, \Theta)$-cyclic codes and their applications in constructing QECCs
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb F_q$ be a finite field, where $q$ is an odd prime power. Let $R=\mathbb{F}_q+u\mathbb{F}_q+v\mathbb{F}_q+uv\mathbb F_q$ with $u^2=u,v^2=v,uv=vu$. In this paper, we study the algebraic structure of $(\theta, \Theta)$-cyclic codes of block length $(r,s )$ over $\mathbb{F}_qR.$ Specifically, we analyze the structure of these codes as left $R[x:\Theta]$-submodules of $\mathfrak{R}_{r,s} = \frac{\mathbb{F}_q[x:\theta]}{\langle x^r-1\rangle} \times \frac{R[x:\Theta]}{\langle x^s-1\rangle}$. Our investigation involves determining generator polynomials and minimal generating sets for this family of codes. Further, we discuss the algebraic structure of separable codes. A relationship between the generator polynomials of $(\theta, \Theta)$-cyclic codes over $\mathbb F_qR$ and their duals is established. Moreover, we calculate the generator polynomials of dual of $(\theta, \Theta)$-cyclic codes. As an application of our study, we provide a construction of quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs) from $(\theta, \Theta)$-cyclic codes of block length $(r,s)$ over $\mathbb{F}_qR$. We support our theoretical results with illustrative examples.

papers.title: Multiset Deletion Codes: Cyclic Syndrome Constructions, Bounds, and Exact Results
papers.abstract: We determine sharp class-size estimates for multiset codes over $q$ symbols that correct up to $t$ deletions. For fixed $q,t\ge2$, we prove that the syndrome classes defined by Nathanson's geometric-sum labels modulo $M=1+t+\cdots+t^{q-1}$ differ from their average size by $O(n^{q/p-1})$, where $n$ is the blocklength and $p$ is the least prime divisor of $q$. This exponent is sharp, and every prescribed class has size asymptotic to the average. For prime $q$, all classes have equal size when $n\equiv-1,\ldots,-(q-1)\pmod M$. We also present our radix construction, whose labels are zero and the first $q-1$ powers of $t+1$, starting at $1$, modulo $t(t+1)^{q-2}+1$. We determine its sharp class-size deviation exponent. For even $q\ge4$, its syndrome classes have a smaller deviation exponent, although their average size is smaller. Over four symbols and every $t\ge2$, we show that the radix labels still correct up to $t$ deletions modulo a reduced modulus, which gives bounded deviations and eventually larger classes than either unmodified construction. For a fixed number $k\ge2$ of surviving symbols, we prove that some maximum code contains all constant words, reducing the remaining optimization to multisets with multiplicities below $k$. Finally, for one deletion at length four over $q\ge4$ symbols, we show that the best bound from fractional weights on deletion outputs, rounded down, equals the maximum code size exactly when $q\equiv2,4\pmod6$.

papers.title: Robust Joint Power Allocation and Antenna Placement for Pinching-Antenna Systems under Gaussian Location Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Pinching antenna systems (PASS) have attracted much attention recently owing to their capability to maintain reliable line-of-sight communication in high-frequency bands. By guiding signals through a waveguide and emitting them via a movable pinching antenna, PASS enable dynamic control of signal propagation and spatial adaptability. However, their performance heavily depends on effective resource allocation, including power allocation and antenna positioning, which becomes challenging under user localization uncertainty. Existing studies largely assume perfect user locations, while our prior work considered uniformly distributed localization errors. In this paper, we develop a robust resource allocation framework for multi-user downlink PASS under Gaussian-distributed localization uncertainty. An energy-efficiency (EE) maximization problem is formulated subject to probabilistic outage constraints, and the minimum transmit power is analytically characterized for any given antenna position. For the unbounded Gaussian model, we prove that the resulting one-dimensional antenna-placement objective is convex and derive a globally optimal derivative-bisection algorithm. We further consider a circularly truncated Gaussian model for bounded localization-error regions and develop a deterministic branch-and-bound method that returns an $\epsilon_{\rm B}$-globally optimal antenna position. Finally, we discuss how position-dependent waveguide attenuation modifies the placement objective and may destroy its convexity. Simulation results verify that the proposed branch-and-bound solution closely matches the bounded grid-search benchmark, demonstrate substantial EE gains from optimized pinching-antenna placement over the bounded fixed-antenna architecture, and reveal an increasing distinction between the bounded and unbounded Gaussian models as the location uncertainty grows.

papers.title: Optimizing Bit-Labeling of Voronoi Constellations
papers.abstract: We optimize the bit-to-symbol map of the $D_4$ and $E_8$ root lattices in reference to bit error rate, by implementing two searches on a performance metric, Hamming Density. The first search is a traditional gradient descent and the second is an efficient search using twisted theta functions. We hold other sources of lattice gain constant by fixing the lattice constellation, and consider basis changes that permute the integer labelings of the lattice points. After searching the possible basis matrices for $D_4$ and $E_8$, we found up to 0.09 dB of gain in $D_4$ bit error rate curves, and up to 0.36 dB of gain in $E_8$ compared to the standard bases commonly used in literature at a BER of $10^{-4}$, which is on the scale of gain from Gray coding uncoded QAMs.

papers.title: Entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes: bounds and constructions with availability
papers.abstract: In this work, we define entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes with availability, in which any set of up to $\delta-1$ erased qudits can be recovered from any one of $t$ local recovery sets, each of size at most $r+\delta-1$, with the recovery sets intersecting exactly in the erased coordinates, where $r$ is a (small) positive integer. We show that shared entanglement permits $t>1$, meaning that multiple local recovery sets can be available for the same set of up to $\delta-1$ erasures. We establish a Singleton-like bound for this family of codes and present random constructions based on classical linear codes with Vandermonde parity-check matrices. We also provide explicit constructions of entanglement-assisted quantum locally recoverable codes with availability from several classical code families and their folded versions, including Tamo-Barg codes, fiber-product codes, and algebraic-geometry codes such as one-point Hermitian and Suzuki codes.

papers.title: Binary Multiple-Node-Erasure-Correcting Codes over Complete Graphs: Constructions, q-Ary Metric Balls, and Duality
papers.abstract: Codes over graphs store symbols on edges of a complete undirected graph on $n$ vertices with a self-loop at each vertex; erasing a node removes all its incident edges. Extending Yohananov, Efron, and Yaakobi's construction, we obtain binary codes correcting any three node erasures at infinitely many prime lengths $n$, unconditionally, with redundancy $3n-2$, one bit above the graph Singleton bound. The earlier construction has the same redundancy but requires $2$ to be primitive modulo $n$, which is not known for infinitely many primes. We give a deterministic decoder for these triple-node codes using $O(n^2)$ binary operations and construct Singleton-optimal binary triple-node codes at $n=6,8,10,12$. When $2$ is primitive modulo an odd prime $n$, we extend their double- and triple-node codes to binary codes correcting $\rho$ node erasures with redundancy $\rho n-(\rho-1)$ for $2\leq\rho\leq(n+1)/2$, saving $\rho-1$ bits over the binary symmetric rank-metric construction when $\rho<(n+1)/2$. Over every finite field of size $q$, the node weight of a word is the least number of vertices whose erasure removes its support. We give exact formulas for ball volumes in this node metric and prove that, for fixed $q,t$, the radius-$t$ volume is asymptotic to $\binom nt q^{tn-\binom t2}$ as $n\to\infty$. We obtain existence and covering bounds; for fixed $q,\rho$, we show that linear $\rho$-node-erasure-correcting codes exist with redundancy at most $\rho\log_q n+O_{q,\rho}(1)$ above the graph Singleton bound. Finally, reformulating Yohananov and Yaakobi's criterion, we show that a linear code over any finite field is Singleton-optimal for $\rho$ node erasures if and only if its dual is Singleton-optimal for erasures of the coordinates inside any $n-\rho$ vertices.
